content: The development process involved four staff members from the Preventing Unsafe Abortion (PUA) Unit within the WHO Department of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Research. Participants included youth leaders (up to age 30) with proven expertise in adolescent sexual and reproductive health and rights, representing 13 countries across WHO regions. Discussions during the meeting focused on three main themes: youth values and preferences regarding abortion services, addressing barriers and stigma associated with abortion, and scaling up promising practices and interventions. Key issues included creating an enabling environment and ensuring meaningful youth engagement. Members of the International Youth Alliance for Family Planning (IYAFP) are preparing a position paper as the primary outcome of the meeting. The Evidence and Recommendations Review Group (ERRG) held online meetings between March 2020 and March 2021, with 4–5 meetings for each of the three domains (clinical services, service delivery, and law and policy). Each meeting spanned two days and was facilitated by WHO technical officers and the WHO Steering Group. During these meetings, systematic reviews of evidence were presented by the Evidence Synthesis Teams, and ERRG members reviewed the evidence, drafted recommendations, and developed implementation considerations and good practice statements. These drafts were later reviewed and finalized by the Guideline Development Group (GDG). The GDG convened online from April 27–30, 2021, to review, revise, and finalize draft recommendations, implementation considerations, and good practice statements across all three domains. These categories included lay health workers, pharmacy workers, pharmacists, traditional and complementary medicine professionals, auxiliary nurse midwives, nurses, midwives, and advanced associate clinicians. Their roles were outlined to reflect their contributions to abortion care and related services. To monitor and evaluate the quality of abortion care, a scoping review and expert consultations were conducted by scientists from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) and WHO. The scoping review identified 792 indicators from 142 documents published between 2008 and 2018. These findings were published in BMJ Global Health, and a subset of 17 core indicators was selected for global and programmatic monitoring. During a consolidation phase, 29 of the 52 proposed indicators were retained, with six new indicators added to address gaps in the health systems monitoring framework. These indicators were categorized into areas such as governance, financing, infrastructure, health workforce, intervention quality, and health outcomes. An online consultation in March 2021 involved 22 experts who reviewed the consolidated indicators. The final indicator list is being finalized and will undergo periodic assessment to maintain relevance. Systematic reviews were conducted to inform recommendations on various topics, including the impact of criminalization, gestational age limits, mandatory waiting periods, and third-party authorization on abortion-related outcomes. Reviews also addressed clinical topics such as pain management, cervical priming, and medical abortion methods. Updated evidence reviews were conducted for topics like prophylactic antibiotics, pre-abortion ultrasound, and surgical methods for first-trimester abortion. Recommendations from previous WHO guidelines were carried forward or updated, including those on post-abortion contraception and the timing of contraceptive initiation. A report summarizing the findings and recommendations will be published in due course.
